<!-- pr-reviewer: 1947b6b6c30d214baf3db2072f95ed51ccb2dae3 -->
Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety-tier review because the PR changes geometry.
I reviewed the PR head after a clean trial merge with upstream main `e048b103ca649e24048268e1a050f0b4686a997a`.
I used the rules from that upstream main.

**What looks good**

- The kernel keeps the raster API and adds no dependencies or ECS access.
- The modules state their sources. The tests cover placement, clearance, quantities, and named refusals.
- The PR changes no UI files, fixtures, or golden files. No moved goldens need a line-by-line check.

**Local results merged with main**

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 937 steps.
Geometry selected the batch fallback.
The build passed. All-targets clippy passed with warnings denied.

| Crate | Tests passed | Tests ignored |
|---|---:|---:|
| geometry | 193 | 0 |
| kernel | 73 | 4 |
| cl | 69 | 0 |
| tools | 145 | 0 |
| post | 821 | 0 |
| sim | 738 | 4 |
| motion | 1196 | 22 |
| app | 3989 | 43 |
| ui | 1431 | 9 |

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 217 steps.
The motion heavy lane passed 56 tests. The app heavy lane passed 42 tests.
Three existing known-fail checks for #1950 failed at their expected assertions: two in motion and one in app.
The gate verified those expected failures. There were no unexpected failures.

After the mutations, the focused geometry run passed all 66 tests again:
51 library tests, five `nesting` tests, four `nesting_modes` tests, and six `nesting_refusals` tests.

**Extra suites run**

The PR changes no fixture or importer files, so those rules require no extra suite.
The batch fallback also ran these named suites:

- Kernel `step_agreement`: 20 passed.
- Kernel `machining_mesh`: seven passed.
- App `feature_edge_g1_join`: five passed.

**Independent mutations**

| Mutation | Pin | With mutation | After restoration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disable exact hole containment | `exact_check_refuses_micron_escape_from_hole` | Failed, exit 101 | Passed |
| Disable exact overlap rejection | `exact_check_refuses_sub_epsilon_overlap` | Failed, exit 101 | Passed |

I restored both mutations. The PR source files have no review changes.

**Requested before merge**

1. `crates/geometry/src/nesting/validate.rs:192` and `:199`: Refuse every non-empty outside or hole-overlap region. These checks accept positive areas at or below `1e-6 mm²`. I reproduced both invalid inputs with zero cut width and zero part gap on a 10 × 10 mm sheet. The outer loop was `[0,1] × [0,1] mm`.

   An escaping hole at `[0.5,1.000001] × [0.2,0.8] mm` produced:

   ```text
   escape: ACCEPTED, placed=1, net_area=1.000000600000
   ```

   The net material area exceeds the outer-loop area. The region normalizer treats this intersecting loop as added material.
   Two holes at `[0.1,0.5] × [0.2,0.8]` and `[0.499999,0.9] × [0.2,0.8] mm` also passed validation:

   ```text
   overlap: ACCEPTED, placed=1, net_area=0.520000600000
   ```

   Both cases must return `NestError::InvalidPart` with the part name.
   Use exact region checks, as in `candidates.rs`, instead of a positive-area allowance.
   Add regression tests for both cases. Run the quick and heavy gates on the fixed head.

**Notes**

The PR body still says that the heavy lanes were not run.
Update that statement with the final-head results when you fix the finding.
No GitHub runner was used. No code, screenshots, logs, or review evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
